![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/8fa5e5b2300c3395d48f5355352cd6ece7477f3bae8e8c185f0f869fa197b0e9.png)

The region enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x$ and the horizontal line $y=2$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curve and the line by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x & =2 \\ {x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x-2 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(x-2)+(x-2) & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}+1)(x-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=2$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/5a1821ff500c901d9f072fe56101f17e579018d0710543c4a2e371214894725c.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=2.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(2)-({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{(2-x+2{x}^{2}-{x}^{3})}^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
